identity.title: LARP: Tokenizing Videos with a Learned Autoregressive Generative Prior

problem.claim: Design a video tokenizer suited to autoregressive generative models.

gap.claim: Existing patchwise tokenizers are described as limited to local patch-level information and not sufficiently aligned with downstream autoregressive generation.

contributions.claim: LARP uses learned holistic queries to tokenize visual content into global, semantic representations rather than directly encoding local patches.
It supports an arbitrary number of discrete tokens and incorporates a lightweight autoregressive transformer as a training-time latent prior.
The training-time prior structures the latent space for autoregressive generation and defines a sequential token order.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish LARP as a novel holistic video tokenizer with a learned autoregressive generative prior.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report state-of-the-art FVD on the UCF101 class-conditional video-generation benchmark.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper frames current video tokenization as limited for autoregressive generation.
LARP replaces local patchwise encoding with learned holistic queries intended to capture global semantic content.
The tokenizer permits an arbitrary number of discrete tokens for task-specific adaptive tokenization.
A lightweight autoregressive transformer is used during training to shape the discrete latent space and token order for generation.
Experiments are reported to achieve state-of-the-art FVD on UCF101 and to support broader multimodal-model ambitions.

source_observation.claim: The abstract explicitly connects the tokenizer’s latent-space design and token ordering to the requirements of downstream autoregressive generation.

lessons.interpretation: A representation can be designed around the structure required by its consuming model, rather than optimized only for reconstruction or local fidelity.
lessons.application: When proposing a learned representation, add a lightweight training-time model that directly reflects the intended downstream factorization, and state which latent properties it is meant to induce.
lessons.exception: This may be unsuitable when the downstream task does not require sequential factorization or when the auxiliary prior materially complicates training.

unknowns: The abstract gives no FVD value, baselines, statistical details, or experimental conditions.
The strength of the claimed generation improvements and the phrase “ensuring” smoother, more accurate inference are not independently verifiable from the abstract.
It does not specify how arbitrary token counts are selected or what trade-offs they create.
